question: What Is Gray Code and How Do You Convert Binary to Gray Code?
body_html:
Gray code is a binary numbering order in which neighbouring values differ in exactly one bit, so a reading taken during a transition is either the old or the new value. It is also called reflected binary code and is used in absolute encoders, Karnaugh maps and FIFO pointers.

To convert, keep the MSB and XOR each neighbouring bit pair: G = B XOR (B shifted right by 1). Example: binary 0111 (7) becomes Gray 0100, and binary 1000 (8) becomes Gray 1100.
